crime: Every evening one prisoner leaned on the upper railing and read the girls' faces in the courtyard below, and by morning a flower stood in each girl's cup. She had learned the knack at her family's flower stall. For {WITCH_NAME} she guessed a different flower every day, and {WITCH_NAME} kept every one under her pillow.

At dinner the flower girl told {WITCH_NAME} kindly, "I read faces, and you hear hearts. But you can't read faces at all, and your own face never tells me if I guessed right. So from tomorrow I'll leave your cup empty rather than guess wrong."

Long ago, {WITCH_NAME}'s mother had written a lunch note for each of her sisters and left hers blank. "I never can tell what you feel, so I don't know what to write." Nobody guesses at a face that shows nothing.

At a quarter to ten, the flower girl leaned out over the railing to watch the last girls go in. {WITCH_NAME} tipped her over, head first onto the rim of the fountain. She took up the basket of flowers the girl had picked. At ten to ten, in the dining hall, she set a flower in each girl's cup, choosing it by the tune she had heard from that girl all evening. The fallen girl's cup got a forget-me-not. Her own she left empty.

At dawn the prisoners found the flower girl dead on the fountain rim. She had never come back to her cell at lockup. Every cup but {WITCH_NAME}'s held a flower, each exactly right. "She said goodbye to each of us," they said, "and jumped."
In the trial court, one prisoner held up the flower from her cup. "This is the one she gave for grief. I smiled through cards all evening and hid my grief from every face. She only ever read faces."
The prisoners understood. Only someone who heard beneath faces could have chosen these flowers. The goodbye was {WITCH_NAME}'s, and so was the push.
fields.epitaph: Every flower under her pillow had been right, because each one was a guess.
fields.epithet: The Face No One Could Guess
execution: In the trial court, a glass cup taller than she was rose up. It stood empty, and she was bound upright at its base among flower stems. Water rose up her body and over her face, her face pressed to the glass. Through it, the spectators watched her face, every feeling plain on it. Then she floated still among the stems, the cup full to the brim.

magic.name: Heartsong
magic.text: She hears each nearby person's mood as music that changes key the instant their mood shifts.
